title: Deployment Safety Harness — experiment canvas and grooming notes
body:
Purpose:
This document collects UX sketches, acceptance criteria, and backlog items for a lightweight 'safety harness' feature in the Rollouts console: a set of controls and visual affordances that make canary/A-B experiments easier to configure and safer to run (automatic fallbacks, traffic guardrails, and probe checks). Goal is a low-friction default that prevents common footguns (silent failures, runaway cost, bad model regressions) while keeping power-user flexibility.

Primary user personas:
- Platform engineer (operator) configuring a canary for a mission-critical endpoint. Wants predictable failover and measurable guardrails.
- Product engineer running A/B experiments on model variants. Wants clear comparison windows and automatic isolation when quality drops.
- SRE on-call who needs rapid insight and one-click mitigation (pause/roll back).

High-level feature components (sketch):
1) Safety Strip (top-level): a horizontal banner on the rollout detail page showing current experiment status (green/yellow/red), most recent probe result, and an action row (Pause / Promote / Revert / Open diagnostics).
2) Traffic Ramp Composer: visual timeline with draggable handles for ramp % over time, with hard-limit caps and an estimated token-cost delta shown live.
3) Probe & Canary Health Panel: configure lightweight probes (sample prompts, latency p95, error rate, safety-linter score). Each probe has threshold sliders (warning/critical) and a source selector (synthetic prompts vs production sampled).
4) Fallback Chain Editor: ordered list of fallback routes (model variant, region, capacity tier). Each fallback node has policy: immediate | graceful (drip) | circuit-breaker with retries/backoff.
5) Experiment Evaluation Window: A/B report settings (metric list, primary metric, required sample size, minimum run time). Auto-stop conditions if metric regression detected.
6) Audit & Explain: inline short logs of automated decisions (why did the harness divert traffic?) with links to query traces.

Wireframe notes / micro-interactions:
- Safety Strip color logic: green = all probes OK and cost within budget; amber = any probe in warning or cost exceeds threshold; red = any critical probe triggered or circuit open. Tooltip on each color with last 3 events.
- Ramp handles snap to 5% increments by default; hold meta to enable 1% increments. When dragging, a thin red overlay will show projected cost burn for the next 24h and a tooltip warns if predicted spend exceeds budget.
- Probe config modal should pre-populate with common templates: "latency p95 < 250ms", "response error rate < 0.5%", "toxicity delta < 1%". Allow user to paste their short test prompts.
- Fallback chain drag-and-drop. Default fallback order should be: compatible model variant in same family -> lower-capacity endpoint (dedicated -> shared) -> region fallback -> error page. Each fallback has a tiny explain icon describing tradeoffs.
- Small inline copy for novices: "Safety Harness will pause or route away from this model when configured thresholds are exceeded. You can always override manually."

Backlog grooming (prioritized):
- P0: Safety Strip status + Pause/Promote/Revert actions (basic gating); basic probe ingestion and display. (Design + backend: 3 weeks)
- P1: Traffic Ramp Composer with cost estimator and preset ramp templates (Design + infra hooks). (2 weeks)
- P1: Fallback Chain Editor (initial: model-variant + region fallback). (2 weeks)
- P2: A/B evaluation window UI + automated stop-on-regression logic (link to Optimize evaluation service). Need stats engine integration for sample-size estimation. (3 weeks)
- P2: Audit explanations and links to traces. (1 week)
- Stretch: Circuit-breaker policy editor with exponential backoff and operator-defined retry budget.

Acceptance criteria / definition of done (for P0):
- Operator can enable Safety Harness on any rollout and see an immediate status tile with last probe values.
- Pause action performs a deterministic traffic cutover to fallback route within SLA (documented).
- Probe definitions stored and surfaced in console; at least two probe types supported (latency, error-rate).
- Unit and integration tests for the gating logic and API surface.

Observability / telemetry to capture:
- Safety Harness activations per rollout, number of automatic pauses in last 30d, time-to-recover after pause, operator overrides.
- Probe-failure events and which fallback route executed.
- Cost delta projection accuracy (predicted vs actual) per rollout.

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve in grooming session:
- Which probe types live in Product vs Require SRE infra? (ex: synthetic prompts may need sampling pipeline).
- Default fallback order: should we surface cost-sensitive defaults (prefer cost saving) or quality-first defaults (prefer highest-quality variant)?
- Should Safety Harness be opt-in per tenant or on by default for all new rollouts?
- How aggressive should auto-stop be for A/B experiments? We want safety but not false positives that break experiments.

Edge cases and constraints:
- Short-lived rollouts (few minutes) may not reach sample size thresholds — provide a banner saying "insufficient sample to evaluate" rather than auto-stop.
- Partial traffic loss in a region: fallback chain should support simultaneous fallbacks (re-route entirely to other region) rather than sequential single-node fallbacks. UX to indicate multi-node action.
- Fail-open vs fail-closed debate: by default harness will fail-open at the route level (re-route to fallback variant) to preserve availability; allow tenant to choose fail-closed for strict isolation customers.

Suggested microcopy for key actions:
- Pause: "Pause this rollout — route new requests to fallback. Existing in-flight requests may finish."
- Promote: "Promote variant to primary for 100% traffic. This changes production model and will be audited."
- Revert: "Revert to last stable model and close this experiment. Requires reason."

Next steps / owners:
- Design: Priya Reddy — deliver hi-fi mockups for Safety Strip, Ramp Composer, Fallback Editor (due 2026-01-12).
- Product: Asha Menon — finalize acceptance criteria and owner for backend contracts (due 2025-11-17).
- Engineering: Diego Alvarez — spike on probe ingestion and sample pipeline; evaluate latency p95 calculation costs (due 2025-12-01).
- SRE: Samir Patel — propose default fallback orders and failure modes for compliance customers (due 2026-01-05).

Notes-to-self / rough ideas to capture in next iteration:
- Could add a 'chaos test' button to intentionally trigger backup behavior in a safe sandbox. Useful for runbook rehearsals.
- Consider small onboarding tour for first-time safety harness users (3 quick steps).
- Integrate with Slack alerts for critical probe triggers with a single "pause rollout" action in the alert.

Links / refs:
- Confluence: rollout-safety-principles (internal) — includes regulatory considerations for fail-closed customers.
- JIRA: JIRA-ROLL-412 — backend work for probe ingestion.
